newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Former U.S. Black Panther to be deported on Friday.
newsitem.headline: Former U.S. Black Panther to be deported on Friday.

text.p: The Australian government on Wednesday rejected two visa applications by former U.S. Black Panther Lorenzo Ervin and said the human rights activist would be deported by Friday.
Ervin, convicted of hijacking an aircraft from the United States to Cuba, was detained by immigration officials on Tuesday pending his expulsion after his first visa was cancelled.

Two new visa applications by Irvin on Wednesday were rejected by Acting Immigration Minister Amanda Vanstone, who said it was not in the national interest for a convicted hijacker to stay in Australia.
"The decision that I have made is one that Mr Ervin is not a person of good character and on that basis I've refused the visa applications," Vanstone told reporters.
When asked when Irvin would be deported, Vanstone said: "I would hope he would be going back on Friday".

Ervin, who was invited to Australia for a four-week speaking tour by anarchist group Angry People, was convicted in the United States in 1969 of hijacking a plane to Cuba. He was given two life sentences, but released from jail in 1983.
Ervin's lawyer Terry Fisher on Wednesday said his client had been granted clemency by the U.S. government and should be allowed to stay in Australia.
Fisher said he had lodged a challenge to the deportation order in Australia's federal court, but no date had been set for a hearing.
Prime Minister John Howard on Monday said Ervin, who arrived on July 4, should never have been allowed into Australia.
Howard said Ervin had apparently misrepresented his past when he applied for a visa to visit Australia and had used a different surname.
Vanstone said Irvin was not picked up by the migration alert system because he used his so-called stage and professional name in his application which did not match with his passport.
Ervin also failed to fill in his passenger entry card indicating that he had been convicted of an offence requiring him to be jailed for more than 12 months, she said.
